audit_scope.basis: Independent formula/specification review against supplied card file and master brief. No implementation repository was supplied; expected cases are an oracle, not executed application tests.
audit_scope.case_design: Five cases per card: two easy, two complex, one edge. Conceptual inputs must be mapped to actual TypeScript schemas without changing intended assertions.

executive_findings.finding: Stored rental fallback is allowed only when rent entries were not handed in (unknown), while DEC-1926 states rental requires a rent entry naming the property. Confirm null/unavailable versus empty list semantics explicitly; do not silently equate missing data with no rent.
All returns must be time-weighted. If a positive holding has unknown gain, a worked-back beginning must refuse and name the holding; do not substitute zero gain or a Dietz return.

Debt minimums are added once, logged debt payments and mortgage budget duplicates are removed, rent offsets monthly draw only when validly mapped, and unknown rent produces qualified months rather than silent assumptions.

Separate face value from current market value; coupon income is face×rate when face exists; current yield and YTM use their respective price bases; bank CDs have no rate-move estimate, broker CDs follow bond pricing; accrued-interest day count and averaging exclusions need helper-backed tests.

Verify account activity sign conventions, no income figure with no transactions, account class totals, cash/investments/property totals, alternatives classified/unclassified split, and component rows summing exactly to totals.
FIFO sale allocation, options multiplier, unknown price vs cost-only value, long-term strictly more than one year, ticker-matched dividends/interest, and realised gain all need integrated tests.

cards.name: gainOfRow
cards.what_it_is_for: THE ONE RULE FOR WHAT A HOLDING GAINED OVER THE WINDOW (DEC-3656, 2026-10-09), or null when it cannot be known.
cards.formula_in_words: What one holding gained over the window, or nothing when that cannot be known. Bought inside the window: its own gain (value less cost). With a return for the period: the return over the WHOLE window (the window total the row carries; else, when the window is longer than one year, the yearly rate compounded over the window's years — (1 + rate) to the power years − 1; else the return as given); then value now × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + that)), and $0 when it holds nothing. A CD with a stated rate above zero: value now × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + the rate) to the power of the window's years), and $0 when it holds nothing. Otherwise: $0 when it holds nothing (heldValueOf is 0), and nothing (unknown) when it holds something or its worth is unknown — a holding with no price history and no rate.

cards.name: theNetWorth
cards.what_it_is_for: What am I worth: everything I own, less everything I owe, and how each breaks down?
cards.formula_in_words: Assets = every account's balance added up. Debts = every debt's remaining balance added up. Net worth = assets − debts. Cash = cashTotal. Investments = investmentsTotal: the investment classes of the class split added up (Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives, Unclassified, from assetAllocation) — so a linked account's uninvested cash is in Cash only, and Cash + Investments + property comes to everything owned. Investable = investableAssets. By class = assetAllocation. Each debt is listed with its balance and its required monthly payment (the larger of its minimum and the payment the person says they make); monthly debt payments = those added up; monthly debt minimum = the minimums alone added up. Return on cash + investments = a TIME-WEIGHTED return (owner decision, 2026-10-04: "All return should be True Weighted Return and not Dietz return.") over every account that is not property: the period from the day compared from to today is split at every day money moved in or out; each piece = the value just before the next movement ÷ the value just after the last one; the pieces are multiplied and 1 is taken off; returned as a share. A month given without a day is read as its first day. Cash earns only interest: any other change in a cash account's balance is money moving, counted on the day the record first shows it. For the other accounts, money moving = deposits, withdrawals and cash transferred between accounts. Today's value is read from the accounts as they stand. No figure when no day is given, when no recorded day on or before the day compared from holds the accounts, when money moved on a day with no recorded value, when a deposit, withdrawal or transfer on a measured account has no amount on record, or when shares were moved in or out. It also hands out the match of mortgages to properties (mortgagesByProperty). It also names the holdings nothing could class and the person has not yet answered about (account, holding), and the sentence that asks. A holding with no price today is taken out of every day of the return's window, the start day included, so the change line leaves it out as the fix sheet promises (Net worth v08 state F).

cards.formula_in_words_reviewed: Assets = every account's balance added up. Debts = every debt's remaining balance added up. Net worth = assets − debts. Cash = cashTotal. Investments = investmentsTotal: the investment classes of the class split added up (Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives, Unclassified, from assetAllocation) — so a linked account's uninvested cash is in Cash only, and Cash + Investments + property comes to everything owned. Investable = investableAssets. By class = assetAllocation. Each debt is listed with its balance and its required monthly payment (the larger of its minimum and the payment the person says they make); monthly debt payments = those added up; monthly debt minimum = the minimums alone added up. Return on cash + investments = a TIME-WEIGHTED return (owner decision, 2026-10-04: "All return should be True Weighted Return and not Dietz return.") over every account that is not property: the period from the day compared from to today is split at every day money moved in or out; each piece = the value just before the next movement ÷ the value just after the last one; the pieces are multiplied and 1 is taken off; returned as a share. A month given without a day is read as its first day. Cash earns only interest: any other change in a cash account's balance is money moving, counted on the day the record first shows it. For the other accounts, money moving = deposits, withdrawals and cash transferred between accounts. Today's value is read from the accounts as they stand. No figure when no day is given, when no recorded day on or before the day compared from holds the accounts, when money moved on a day with no recorded value, when a deposit, withdrawal or transfer on a measured account has no amount on record, or when shares were moved in or out. It also hands out the match of mortgages to properties (mortgagesByProperty). It also names the holdings nothing could class and the person has not yet answered about (account, holding), and the sentence that asks. A holding with no price today is taken out of every day of the return's window, the start day included, so the change line leaves it out as the fix sheet promises (Net worth v08 state F).

cards.name: theEmergencyFund
cards.what_it_is_for: How many months of essential expenses would my cash cover?
cards.formula_in_words: Cash = all cash (cashTotal), or the amount handed in when one is given. Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "Once user enters mortgage or any debt - the app deduct it directly to calculate surplus, emergency fund, and any other place instead of leaving it for user to add it to planned expenses." Debt minimums = the MINIMUM monthly payment of every debt added up — the home's mortgage included; a balance due in one lump has none. A payment a person chooses to make above the minimum is not counted: it can be stopped. The budget is read as it is counted (theBudgetCounted): where the home's mortgage is in Debts, the Rent / Mortgage budget line is counted as nothing, and the screen is given a sentence saying so. Essentials for a month = essential expenses + debt minimums. Essential expenses = the average of what was logged, over the calendar months of the last twelve that have a logged entry (this month alone when only it has one); the typed plan only when nothing is logged. Left out of that average, so nothing is counted twice: a payment logged against a debt that is entered (an expense in the category Debt payment, named for that debt), and, where the home's mortgage is in Debts, anything logged under Rent / Mortgage. Rent that keeps arriving = the Rent row of the Income summary (rent from a property less what it costs to run, less calculated tax when the tax rate is calculated), never below zero; owner, 2026-10-04: "add it to the cash as losing job does not mean loosing rental income too." It arrives every month, so it is added to the cash every month. From cash each month = essentials − that rent, never below zero. Months covered = cash ÷ from cash each month; no figure when essentials are zero, and no figure when the rent pays for the whole month (the cash is then not drawn on, and it says so). Planned = planned monthly expenses + debt minimums; months covered at the planned level = cash ÷ (planned − that rent); no figure when that is zero or less. Target for N months = from cash each month × N; gap = target − cash, never below zero. Months left after a shock = (cash − the shock, never below zero) ÷ from cash each month. When a typed month of essentials is handed in, it stands in for essentials + debt minimums. A target, and the months left after a shock, are given only when there is an essentials figure. Rent not known, owner rule 2026-10-10 (instead of showing nothing, the card says the months are counted with the rent not included, and asks for the rent): the answer also says whether a property's rent is not known. It is not known only when the household holds a property that is not the home (home, rental and second home read by the owner's property-use rule of 2026-10-04) AND one of these holds: a rent entry's rent figure is blank or not a plain number, or the entry names no property (it is not counted as rent, owner rule DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10); with no list of rent entries, the single typed rent figure is typed at all (it names no property, so it is not counted, DEC-4059d); the rent entries are stored in a shape that is not a list; or with no rent entries stored at all, a property is kept as a rental. A property with no rent entry when rent entries are stored is a second home, not a missing rent. A household with no property other than the home is never flagged. The months covered are still given, counted without the unknown rent.

cards.name: theHolding
cards.what_it_is_for: How is this one holding doing: its value, its cost, and its gains realised and not yet realised?
cards.formula_in_words: Shares = shares of every purchase still held, added up (nothing when a purchase has no share count); a sale has already taken its shares from the purchases, oldest purchase date first (a purchase with no date last). Total paid = shares × cost per share over every purchase (× 100 for an option contract unless the holding states its own multiplier); nothing when a share count or a cost is not on record. With a price: value = shares × price (× 100 for an option contract unless the holding states its own multiplier); gain = value − total paid; return on cost = gain ÷ total paid (no figure when nothing was paid, or either is unknown). With NO price: value shown = total paid, and gain, return and the tax estimate are not given. Average paid per share = total paid ÷ (shares × that multiplier), so it is in the unit the price is quoted in (nothing with no shares, or a figure not on record). Closed = shares known and zero or less. Day change = last close − the close before, for ONE share (it is shown under the price of one share, not multiplied by shares held), and that ÷ the close before; none with fewer than two closes. Gain if sold today is split by purchase: long-term = purchases held MORE than one year; a purchase held exactly one year or less is short-term. Dividends = dividend records that name this ticker: the last 365 days, and all time. Realised gain = from the sale records of this ticker in this account, × this holding's contract multiplier.

With NO price: value shown = total paid, and gain, return and the tax estimate are not given. Average paid per share = total paid ÷ (shares × that multiplier), so it is in the unit the price is quoted in (nothing with no shares, or a figure not on record). Closed = shares known and zero or less. Day change = last close − the close before, for ONE share (it is shown under the price of one share, not multiplied by shares held), and that ÷ the close before; none with fewer than two closes. Gain if sold today is split by purchase: long-term = purchases held MORE than one year; a purchase held exactly one year or less is short-term. cards.name: thePerformance
cards.what_it_is_for: How are my investments doing over a period: where they started, what I put in and took out, what they made, where they ended, and the return?
cards.formula_in_words: Records of the period = those dated on or after its first day; contributions, withdrawals, dividends and interest are their totals. Contributions also count cash or shares transferred in from an account that is not one of those measured, and the first recorded value of an account that joined the record inside the period (its own records up to that day are then not counted again); withdrawals also count cash or shares transferred out. A transfer between two measured accounts is neither. THE BEGINNING IS READ from the daily record at the day BEFORE the period opens, and only when investment accounts are named and the record's first day is on or before that day; the value read is the last recorded day on or before it. If it cannot be read and the record holds days for these accounts that begin after the period opens: NO walk (no beginning, no wealth generated), and a sentence: The record begins <its first day>, so it cannot say what this account was / these accounts were worth on <the day before the period>. If it cannot be read and there is no record of these accounts at all: beginning = ending − priced gain − contributions + withdrawals (priced gain counts as 0 when the period opens today). The priced gain is each holding's gain over the period by the one rule for it (pricedGainOf: a holding's return is read as the period's own total, never a yearly rate), years = the period's days ÷ 365; a measured account with no holdings counts as its own holding, worth its balance — a certificate of deposit stating its rate gains by that rate, any other has no price history. With no period at all (day one) no rate is applied and a holding with no price history adds nothing. Owner decision DEC-3656, 2026-10-09: where a period is given that does not open today and any holding's gain cannot be known (it holds something, has no price history and no stated rate): NO walk (no beginning, no wealth generated), and the sentence: The beginning can't be worked back: <name> has no price history. Several names are joined with commas and "and" before the last, and say "have no price history". A holding is named by its ticker (the security's name where the ticker is a 9-character identifier); an account by its display name; a dollar gain handed in as unknown is named "a holding". Either way NO percent of any kind is given. The ending is given on its own as well, whether or not there is a walk. Walk: wealth generated = ending − beginning − contributions + withdrawals; change in investment value = wealth generated − dividends − interest. Records counted are those of the investment accounts named (a record on any other account is not money put into these investments). Return = a TIME-WEIGHTED return (owner decision, 2026-10-04: "All return should be True Weighted Return and not Dietz return."): the period, starting at the last recorded day on or before the day before it opens, is split at every day money moved in or out of those accounts; each piece = the value just before the next movement ÷ the value just after the last one; the pieces are multiplied and 1 is taken off. The record holds one value a day, taken after that day's money moved; money that moves on a day counts for that whole day (owner decision DEC-4439, 2026-10-11), so a day's link = that day's value ÷ (the previous recorded day's value + money added that day − money taken out that day). Money moving = deposits (in), withdrawals (out), cash transferred between accounts (out of the first, into the second), and shares moved in or out at what they were worth (the amount, or shares × price) when the record says which way they went. Ending = what the measured accounts are worth today, each counted whole (its balance, uninvested cash inside it included), read from the accounts handed in — a figure handed in beside them is not used, so no two screens can give two endings; with no accounts handed in, the ending handed in is used and closes the record. Today's value for the return is read from the same accounts. An account that first appears in the record inside the period counts as money in, at its first recorded value. A recorded day that is missing an account with holdings is not used; a typed balance stands until it is next recorded. It REFUSES — no percent, a sentence saying why, never another method — when: the beginning cannot be read; money moved on a day with no recorded value; a movement has no date; a deposit, withdrawal or transfer has no amount on record; shares were moved in or out and the record does not say which way or what they were worth; the previous recorded day's value + the money moved that day is zero or less while that day holds a value (nothing to grow from); or nothing was invested. For a period longer than one year — its first day earlier than one year back from today by the calendar (windowStartKey), so a period opening one year back to the day is a year and is never made yearly — and days ÷ 365 above 1, unless it is the whole-record Since period, the figure shown is the yearly rate (1 + return) to the power 1 ÷ years, − 1.

A recorded day that is missing an account with holdings is not used; a typed balance stands until it is next recorded. It REFUSES — no percent, a sentence saying why, never another method — when: the beginning cannot be read; money moved on a day with no recorded value; a movement has no date; a deposit, withdrawal or transfer has no amount on record; shares were moved in or out and the record does not say which way or what they were worth; the previous recorded day's value + the money moved that day is zero or less while that day holds a value (nothing to grow from); or nothing was invested. For a period longer than one year — its first day earlier than one year back from today by the calendar (windowStartKey), so a period opening one year back to the day is a year and is never made yearly — and days ÷ 365 above 1, unless it is the whole-record Since period, the figure shown is the yearly rate (1 + return) to the power 1 ÷ years, − 1.
